coverage.evidence: Q6-3 shows the para-bromophenyl quinol reacting with para-lithio/para-OTBS biphenyl after NaH. Standard carbonyl addition and implicit work-up give Br–phenylene–1,4-dihydroxycyclohexadiene–phenylene–phenylene–OTBS. The theorem evaluates this source-transcribed addition to structureF and checks C30H33BrO3Si and the complete graph invariants.

The printed TESCl (2 equiv.)/imidazole step protects both free alcohols of F. structureG contains two OTES groups while retaining the terminal OTBS ether and bromide; the theorem checks C42H61BrO3Si3 and the expanded graph.

The LiOH step exposes the terminal phenol while retaining the two OTES groups. The resulting Br–P–D(OTES,OTES)–P–P–OH graph has C36H47BrO3Si2, exactly the formula printed beside H; the theorem proves the reaction-prefix equality and graph checks.

The source specifies aqueous PhI(OAc)2 as a two-electron oxidant. Standard para-phenol oxidative dearomatization gives the terminal para-hydroxycyclohexadienone represented in structureI, with the earlier protected diene and bromide unchanged. The theorem checks C36H47BrO4Si2 and the full graph.

Q6-3 shows NaH followed by para-bromophenyllithium. Carbonyl addition/work-up converts I's terminal cyclohexadienone into a second 1,4-diol masked phenylene bearing a terminal para-bromophenyl group. The theorem derives structureJ and checks C42H52Br2O4Si2 and all graph invariants.

The second TESCl (2 equiv.)/imidazole step protects the two newly formed alcohols while the first two OTES groups remain unchanged. structureK therefore has four OTES groups and two terminal bromides; the theorem checks C54H80Br2O4Si4 and the exact graph.

The Ni(COD)2/2,2'-bipyridine step joins the two aryl carbons bearing Br, removes both terminal bromides, and closes the five-unit macrocycle. structureL has the exact printed formula C54H80O4Si4. structure_l proves the closure result and graph checks; structure_l_gives_five_cpp additionally verifies that fourfold TES removal and reductive aromatization yield cyclic C30H20 [5]CPP.
